audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[].side read 'Skill' while content win[] reads Karma x4 then Malzahar x3, matching the packet chart.
audit.why: Karma's 950 Q against a 900 Q on an immobile target wins the poke war before 6; Nether Grasp and free Malefic Visions waveclear own everything after.
audit.corrected: Sides aligned to content/packet as one atomic group; phases[4..6].why rewritten to argue the Malzahar verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4..6].why described Karma's own spikes on rows the chart gives Malzahar, and no spike carried a number.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140/110/80s — a 140-second rank-1 cooldown is the single most exploitable window in this lane and it appeared nowhere.
audit.corrected: Level 6 = Nether Grasp at 140s; first item = free Malefic Visions waveclear; 2+ items = Void Shift CC immunity plus a fight-ending suppression.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's own defect note says the page never names a single Malzahar ability, and the three decisive interactions were all absent: Nether Grasp is a channel your W root cancels; Call of the Void silences at 900 range, which turns off your shield, root and Mantra; Void Shift is damage reduction plus CC immunity until he takes damage. dosFull[0].d and report[5].t also called Void Shift a 'passive shield'.
audit.why: All three are in Riot's text/flags and all three are listed in missingInteractions here.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, winCon, enemyWin, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d, report[5].t and spikes[1].text; 'passive shield' corrected to what Void Shift actually is.

audit.why: The whole page told you to play around Nether Grasp's cooldown without ever stating it.
audit.corrected: Nether Grasp 140s, Call of the Void 6s at 900 range, plus what Void Shift does and when it lapses.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two copy-paste-bleed bullets (dosFull[1].d = tradeGood, dontsFull[2].d = tradeBad); whys[6] claimed his combo has 'no counterplay', which contradicts his R being an interruptible channel.
audit.why: The bullet titles promised poking last-hits and trading at his range; the 'no counterplay' line would teach a paying reader to hold a root that would have saved them.
audit.corrected: Both bullets rewritten to their titles; whys[6] and spikes[1].text now name the counterplay.

notes: The packet's defect note ('never names any of Malzahar's abilities') is now addressed: Void Shift, Call of the Void, Malefic Visions and Nether Grasp all appear with what they actually do. Two factual corrections: Void Shift was described as a 'passive shield' in two fields — it is damage reduction plus CC immunity that lapses when he takes damage — and whys[6] claimed the suppress combo has 'no counterplay' while his R carries the channel flag, so a W root ends it. All seven phases[].side read 'Skill' against a content win[] matching the packet chart; the sides are one atomic group and win[] already holds the target values, so no paired content edit exists. I did not write anything about Cleanse or QSS against suppression — that is not in the kit text.
